events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body: The driver cancelled this RydeX booking and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to the rider [F4][F7]. Under NS-0 a driver-cancelled trip with a no-show allegation is routed through NS-1 / NS-2, so the fee can only stand if all three NS-1 conditions hold [NS-0]. Condition (i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:45 [F6], and condition (ii) is satisfied because the tap occurred 41 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1]. Condition (iii) fails: although the driver was within 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 30 s before cancelling [F2], the tap-to-cancellation window inside the radius was only 2 min 55 s (175 s) [F6], which is not more than 3 minutes as NS-1(iii) requires [NS-1]. The platform's own arrival timestamp (13:01:10, cancelled 4 min 30 s later) [F5] does not repair this, because NS-1(iii) measures waiting from the "I'm Here" tap, and the trace settles that element as failed. Because NS-1 (iii) is not met, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 must be refunded in full [NS-2]. The rider's account (0 disputes in 90 d) and the driver's profile (0 upheld disputes, rating 4.81) [F16][F17] do not affect this outcome: profile facts never decide a case on their own [NS-1][NS-2]. The fare record shows the fee charged was $6.61 with no surge component [F7][F8], so the refund amount is the full $6.61. The congestion record (speed band 3, 20–29 km/h) [F13] and the fair weather [F15] are irrelevant to a no-show fee, and no traffic incident was recorded [F14]; the driver's post-trip statement that he waited more than 3 minutes [F12] is contradicted by the timeline record, which takes precedence [F6][NS-1]. No account flag is warranted: the trace shows the "I'm Here" tap was genuine (41 m from pickup) [F6][F1], so NS-2's anti-fraud limb does not trigger.

There is no action against your account — the tap was inside the pickup area and was not treated as fraudulent, so nothing changes for you. No voucher or payment is owed by you; the refund is covered by Ryde. Questions about this outcome are welcome.
